events.title: Release Date Announcement

events.title: Celestial Golf in Steam Next Fest
events.summary: The Celestial Golf demo will be featured in Steam Next Fest starting tomorrow (October 19)! This is a huge moment as it represents essentially the final, polished vision for the game, cut down into a short demo.If you have already played the demo, thank you! The update going out now adds a bunch of polish and some sneak previews at what's to come when the full game launches. Since the demo has been out for about a year, you might find all sorts of new things have been added since you last played

events.title: Small update: Shorter Daily Challenges
events.summary: A quick update:Daily Challenge: Reduced the number of holes from 9 to 5. This is in response to some player feedback that nine holes was a bit long to do in a single sitting.

events.title: The Daily Challenge Update
events.summary: I've been hard at work on the later levels of the game in preparation for launch before the end of 2026! As such, today's update is fairly light on changes for the demo content, but there is one major headline feature: a new Daily Challenge mode for advanced players.Daily ChallengeThe Daily Challenge is a brand new game mode which presents you with a randomly generated 9-hole course spread across the solar system each day. events.summary: This update is a very special one, because we start to see some of the game's story unfold, told through some short cutscenes and dialogue.Headlining this update are two short cutscenes to bring the world of Celestial Golf to life.The first cutscene plays when the game launches, and explains how the sport was first invented in the 1970s. After playing for some amount of time, UI and game elements would disappear or start showing garbage. events.title: Minor hotfix
events.summary: This is a quick hotfix for the following issue which was introduced in the 0.8 release:Fixed inability to click the Reset Camera button with the mouse.

events.title: The "Challenge Accepted" Update
events.summary: The Celestial Golf demo has a major new update today. This update introduces a new optional challenge system, putting your orbital skills to the test to try and minimize the amount of time or power it takes to complete each hole.In addition to the usual golf "par" (for the number of strokes you took), each hole now has a "time par" and a "power par". events.title: The Performance Update
events.summary: A minor update to the demo, but it contains major performance improvements, particularly on low-end hardware. (My old laptop is much happier after this update!)Performance updateTrajectory computation: impact with distant bodies (any body other than the current sphere of influence) is now estimated based on a circular radius, rather than calculated precisely. events.title: Minor hotfix
events.summary: A quick patch fixing a crash when clicking Free Play on the main menu. (This only affects the unreleased retail version, not the publicly available demo.)

events.title: The Controller Update
events.summary: Grab your controller or Steam Deck because Celestial Golf just got updated with full (experimental) controller support! Controller supportI have just done a complete overhaul of the control scheme when using a game controller. The game is now fully playable and tutorialized for controller (just touch any button to switch input prompts and tutorials over to controller mode). I would love to hear your feedback on anything you find difficult to control in this mode, what you think could be improved

events.title: Devlog: How I redesigned the game's tutorial
events.summary: Celestial Golf needs a detailed tutorial to teach you how to manipulate orbital trajectories, but the first attempt was too verbose and filled up too much of the screen. In this video, I walk through how I redesigned the tutorial system in response to player feedback.I originally designed a single combined system to teach controls, concepts and add a bit of flavour. events.title: Devlog: A plan to fix the game's UI
events.summary: Thanks to everyone who playtested the game (which, as a reminder, is available to anyone by clicking "Join the Playtest").In this devlog update, I go over some of the difficulties of getting playtesting feedback, and how I plan to improve the game's UI, especially with regards to the "time preview" feature which is frustrating to use.

events.title: Devlog: Making Planets
events.summary: In today's Celestial Golf developer update, I show how I created the realistic planet surfaces in the game using Blender.The game is 2D, so we aren't importing the full 3D mesh into the game, but rendering it into a colour and normal map, so we can get realistic dynamic lighting provided by Godot's 2D renderer. I show how I go from getting the NASA terrain data, through construction and rendering in Blender, and importing into Godot.

events.title: Devlog: How I faked rotating planets using the centrifugal/coriolis forces
events.summary: I just published a new video devlog about how I make the planets appear to rotate in Godot:I'm trying a bit of a shorter format (6 minutes) so hopefully it's a bit tighter than the previous ones.My early experiments with the ball bouncing on spinning planets didn't go so well, so instead, I make the planets stationary and pretend they are rotating, by applying the centrifugal and coriolis forces to the ball. I have a lot of fun playing with the loopy trajectories in this video. Enjoy!

events.title: New gameplay reveal video
events.summary: I just posted the first in-depth gameplay video showing me playing the current build of Celestial Golf:A detailed playthrough of a couple of missions, going from the Moon to Earth, and then from Earth to Mars.Check it out, and subscribe to the YouTube channel for more devlogs.
